summary: Morgan Hill sits at the southern end of the Santa Clara Valley, bracketed by the Santa Cruz Mountains to the west and the Diablo Range to the east, which means sunset views here aren't blocked by neighboring rooftops — they're filtered through ridgelines that glow amber most of the year, thanks to roughly 9.4 hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 71°F that make the climate feel more like the Central Coast than the fog-prone Bay. Despite its position inside Silicon Valley's gravitational pull, this is not a major job center; most employment runs toward agriculture, light industry, and the service economy anchoring a small but walkable downtown along Monterey Road, while the tech campuses that pay the region's outsized salaries sit 20-plus miles north along U.S. 101. That commute reality shows up in the numbers: a median household income of nearly $160K sounds enormous until you compare it to median home values above $1.1 million — a price-to-income ratio around 7:1, meaning even high earners face steep leverage to buy. The 3.9% poverty rate and relatively low violent-crime rate of 238 per 100K suggest economic stability, and the surrounding open space — including trails threading into Henry W. Coe State Park and the foothills east of town — offers genuine rural-edge access within minutes. Morgan Hill is essentially a small agricultural town that absorbed Silicon Valley pricing without fully absorbing Silicon Valley jobs, and that gap defines nearly every financial decision made here.
